purpose: You build series by hand: a list and its running total, the Gauss pairing, shift and subtract, sigma notation, and partial sums that settle or do not. Bars and formulas are shown side by side so you can see they agree.

stops.title: The picture
stops.text: The figure changes with the view you pick. Blue bars are terms, yellow marks are running totals, violet dashed lines are special values such as a limit. Every number is an exact fraction or whole number.
stops.try: Press Next in the steps and watch the figure change from bars to rows to partial sums.

stops.title: Choose a view
stops.text: Six views: running total, pairing the ends, shift and subtract, adding forever, the sigma machine and a bouncing ball. Each has its own sliders.
stops.try: Pick The sigma machine, then drag Start of k and End of k and count the terms.

stops.title: Reverse and stack
stops.text: In Pair up the ends, this adds the list written backwards in red on top of the blue list. Every column then reaches the same height a1 + an.
stops.try: Switch it on, then press Gauss: 1 to 100.

stops.title: Pick the ratio r
stops.text: r is the number each term is multiplied by. Try 1/2, 2 and -1. The value 1 is the trap: the formula would divide by zero, so the sum is just n times a1.
stops.try: In Shift and subtract, choose 1 (the trap) and read the red line.

stops.title: Predict, then see
stops.text: In Adding forever, you commit to a guess about the partial sums before more bars appear. The explanation says why, using whether r is between -1 and 1.
stops.try: Pick an answer, then slide Number of terms and compare.

stops.title: Practice
stops.text: Eleven fixed problems. Pick an answer on the buttons. A wrong pick explains the mistake and lets you try again. Nothing is saved or scored.
stops.try: Press Start practice and answer problem 1.

stops.title: Steps
stops.text: Four steps: sequence versus series, pairing the ends, shift and subtract, adding forever. Each step sets up the figure; you then change it yourself.
stops.try: Go through all four, then open the sigma machine and the bouncing ball from the menu.

stops.title: Quick check
stops.text: Three questions: what a series is, a sigma calculation with a start index, and spotting a wrong use of the infinite formula. A wrong answer explains why.
stops.try: Try the third question and use the hint if you are stuck.

teacher: Use it after sequences. Ask: why does every column reach the same height, and why do we halve? Watch for n-1 versus n terms, forgetting to halve, using a1/(1-r) when |r| is 1 or more, and thinking an infinite sum means you finish adding.
